_comment: Factory names and their numInputs, enumerated empirically against MoI 4.0 by calling moi.command.createFactory on every candidate name (createFactory throws 'Invalid function argument 1' on an unknown name). This is the authoritative list: it found six factories no published source lists. numInputs is the count at creation time - factories in the curve family start at 0 and grow as createInput is called. See docs/research/probe-07-factory-coverage.md.

notes.curve: Inputs are built at runtime, not fixed. Call createInput('point') once per vertex and set each. See DoCurve.js.
notes.interpcurve: Inputs are built at runtime, not fixed (numInputs is 0). Call createInput('point') once per vertex and set each. MoI's own script calls DoCurve('interpcurve', true), which also creates a bool input for the corner flag. See DoCurve.js.
notes.polyline: createInput('point') once per vertex, set each, then update() and commit(). No bool inputs - DoCurve.js is called with docorners false. getCreatedObjects() stays empty here; capture the result by diffing the scene.
notes.sketchcurve: Driven by a point-stream picker (createPointStreamPicker().bind(factory)), not by setInput. Not usefully scriptable.
notes.scale: 0 objects, 1 frame, 2 scale factor, 3 reference point 1, 4 reference point 2, 5 bool. See DoScale.js.
notes.scale1d: Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 Origin (point), 2 Scale factor (number), 3 Ref A (point), 4 Ref B (point), 5 Make copies (bool). See DoScale.js, called as DoScale('scale1d', ...).
notes.scale2d: Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 Origin (frame), 2 Scale factor (number), 3 Ref A (point), 4 Ref B (point), 5 Make copies (bool). See DoScale.js, called as DoScale('scale2d', ...).
notes.scalenonuniform: Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 OriginFrame (frame), 2 XScale (number), 3 YScale (number), 4 ZScale (number). No stock script uses it.
notes.cylinder: From a script, set 4 End pt (point) for the height: 5 Height (number) alone is ignored and calculate() returns a flat circle (type 2, zero Z extent), not a solid, with no error. Inputs: 0 Is radius (bool), 1 Base pt (frame), 2 Radius pt, 3 Radius, 4 End pt, 5 Height. See probe-12.
notes.cone: From a script, set 4 End pt (point) for the height: 5 Height (number) alone is ignored and calculate() returns a flat circle (type 2, zero Z extent), not a solid, with no error. Inputs: 0 Is radius (bool), 1 Base pt (frame), 2 Radius pt, 3 Radius, 4 End pt, 5 Height. See probe-12.
notes.arrow3d: No stock script uses it. Inputs: 0 Start pt (point), 1 End pt (point).
notes.calcarea: A measurement, not geometry. Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 Area (number, the result). No stock script uses it.
notes.calclength: Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 Length (number, the result). No stock script uses it.
notes.calcvolume: Inputs: 0 Objects (objects), 1 Volume (number, the result). No stock script uses it.
notes.drag: Inputs: 0 Objects, 1 Base pt, 2 Offset pt, 3 Make copies (bool), 4 Distance from edge (number), 5 From edge cplane (frame). No stock script uses it; prefer 'move'.
notes.label: Inputs: 0 Pt (point), 1 Label (string). No stock script uses it.
notes.objectframerotate: Drives the interactive object-frame gizmo. Inputs: 0 Objects, 1 Frame, 2 Width, 3 Height, 4 WhichGrip (int), 5 DragBasePt, 6 RefPt, 7 Dim (int), 8 Make copies, 9 From Corner, 10 Enable mirror copy. Prefer 'rotate' or 'rotateaxis' from a script.
notes.objectframerotatewheel: Inputs: 0 Objects, 1 Frame, 2 Make copies (bool). Interactive gizmo; prefer 'rotateaxis'.
notes.objectframescale: Drives the interactive object-frame gizmo, for scaling. Inputs: 0 Objects, 1 Frame, 2 Width, 3 Height, 4 WhichGrip (int), 5 DragBasePt, 6 RefPt, 7 Dim (int), 8 Make copies, 9 From Corner, 10 Enable mirror copy. Prefer 'scale' or 'scalenonuniform' from a script.

_introspection: Every factory input describes itself: getInput(i).name is a human label and .type is a code - 1 point, 2 frame, 3 bool, 4 number, 5 int/enum, 6 string, 8 objects (9 seen on loft's Orientations and chamfer's Corners, meaning unconfirmed - see probe-11). moi_factory_help reads these live, so it answers for all 110 factories whether or not a stock script happens to use them.
